summary: Mutual Halyard-template NDA with Dutch counterparty edits that widen the Purpose and use right, narrow the carve-outs (deleting independent development), add a 24-month non-solicit, and raise 18-month survival and Dutch-law requests.

findings.quote: VLIET & VAN DER BERG ADVIES B.V., a private company with limited liability
findings.why: Counterparty entity details were filled in (Dutch B.V., KvK 74829103); this is an entity-detail correction, not covered by a rule, so the lawyer must confirm it against the company register.

findings.quote: [[INS: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time]]
findings.why: The Purpose is widened to 'any other internal or external business activities', which is effectively an open-ended purpose rather than a potential commercial relationship.
findings.draft_redline: (A) The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the Purpose to discussions about a potential commercial relationship between the Parties so that the use of confidential information stays clearly limited. If a specific project or evaluation is intended, we are happy to name it.

findings.quote: [[INS: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation]]
findings.why: The insertion permits use of Confidential Information for the Receiving Party's own internal assessment, benchmarking and market evaluation, and 'solely' is deleted, so use is no longer limited to the Purpose.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep use of Confidential Information limited solely to the Purpose, so we have restored the original wording of clause 2.1.2.

findings.quote: either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition is limited to information disclosed for the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information, and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is raised from 'written records or other reasonable evidence' to 'contemporaneous documentary' evidence, which narrows every carve-out and is not the accepted written-records or reasonable-evidence standard.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1 The obligations set out in Clause 2 shall not apply to any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the evidence standard as 'written records or other reasonable evidence', which we think is workable for both Parties.

findings.quote: [[INS: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement]]
findings.why: The already-lawfully-held carve-out is narrowed so it only applies if shown by written records dated before the Agreement date, a stricter test than the accepted 'written records or reasonable evidence'.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.2 was already lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, free from any restriction as to its use or disclosure;
findings.note_to_counterparty: The evidence standard in the lead-in to clause 3.1 already covers this point, so we have removed the additional dating requirement.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: The independent-development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required carve-outs is missing.
findings.draft_redline:
3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Independent development is a standard exception that protects both Parties, so we have reinstated clause 3.1.4.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis with the recipient liable for them.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to the minimum extent required by an order of any court of competent jurisdiction
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and the backup and legal-retention exceptions in 6.2 with continuing confidentiality in 6.3 all match the preferred position.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is use for the Purpose, but note this depends on the Purpose staying narrow (see the PB03 findings).

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is provided 'as is' with a mutual no-warranty statement.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.]]
findings.why: The reliance exclusion is reworded more widely and wordily but keeps the fraud carve-out, and it applies to whichever Party is the Disclosing Party.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall oblige either Party to disclose any particular information, to enter into any further agreement or transaction with the other Party
findings.why: Includes the preferred no-obligation-to-proceed statement.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction needing prior written consent, with a legal-requirement exception.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: No personal data beyond business contact details, and any other sharing only after a separate DPA or data sharing agreement.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early is the preferred position.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure. Please confirm if Clause 10.3 can be amended accordingly.
findings.why: The counterparty asks for survival of 18 months, which is below the 2-year minimum and the clause 10.3 text itself (3 years plus Trade Secrets) is otherwise unchanged, so this request must be escalated.
findings.draft_redline: 10.3 The obligations of confidentiality and non-use contained in this Agreement shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination, save that in respect of any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret, such obligations shall continue in full force and effect for so long as that information remains a Trade Secret under applicable law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for raising this. We are able to consider a shorter survival period of no less than two years, provided Trade Secrets remain protected for as long as they are Trade Secrets; 18 months is shorter than we can agree and we will revert once reviewed.

findings.quote: neither Party shall, and each Party shall procure that no member of its Group shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel
findings.why: A new non-solicit runs for the term plus 24 months (over 12 months), has no general-advertising exception, and covers consultants and senior staff of the whole Group, also catching those merely contacted or written about.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 10.4 and the definition of Key Personnel in clause 1.1.9.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not agree to a non-solicitation covenant in a confidentiality agreement, so we have removed clause 10.4 and the related definition. The Parties remain bound by the confidentiality terms in respect of any staff information shared.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual 'entitled to seek' equitable relief, with cumulative remedies in 11.2.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner
findings.why: No assignment by either Party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: As we are headquartered in Amsterdam, our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11. Would Halyard be amenable to this?
findings.why: The counterparty asks for Dutch governing law and exclusive Amsterdam courts, which is a deviation from English law and courts; the clause text itself is unchanged.
findings.draft_redline:
12.10 ... shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
12.11 Each Party irrevocably agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim ...
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for raising this. We are unable to agree to Dutch law and courts, but as a compromise we can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Text still gives English law and exclusive English courts, as preferred.
